heading: Back to bare, then sealed up.
lede: Stain or paint, after a good wash and a few dry days. If a board needs to be replaced, we'll tell you.
includes: Washing off dirt, green growth, and old loose finish
Fixing popped nails and screws so no one trips
Stain or paint, whichever is best for your wood

faq.question: Should I stain it or paint it?
faq.answer:
Stain soaks into the wood. When it wears, we wash it and add more. Paint sits on top and looks solid, but when it wears out it peels.

For most deck floors, stain is easier to take care of. We'll look at your wood and tell you what we'd do.

faq.question: How long after washing can you stain?
faq.answer: Usually two or three dry days. If it's been damp, it may take longer. We want the wood dry first.

faq.question: What if some boards are rotten?
faq.answer: We'll show you. We don't replace boards ourselves. Some people have a carpenter fix a few boards first, then we come in.

faq.question: How often does a deck need redoing?
faq.answer: It depends on sun, weather, and how much it gets used. When we finish, we'll tell you what to watch for.

steps.title: Wash it
steps.body: Dirt, green growth, and old peeling finish come off. This makes a big difference.

steps.title: Let it dry
steps.body: We wait two or three dry days. Sealing wet wood traps the water inside.

steps.title: Sand and fix
steps.body: We sand rough boards and fix popped nails. If a board is soft or rotten, we'll point it out.

steps.title: Stain or paint
steps.body: We go along the full length of each board so there are no lap marks. Then we let it dry before you use it.

stepsLede: Deck stain fails when the wood isn't clean or isn't dry. So we take care of both first.
